44744-superstition-in-medicine.title: In Medicine
44744-superstition-in-medicine.creator: Prof. Dr. Hugo Magnus
44744-superstition-in-medicine.description: A book by Prof. Dr. Hugo Magnus. always called forth a feeling of impotency and dependence in the human mind. This consciousness of being dependent upon factors which are entirely beyond human understanding has thus given rise to the metaphysical need of reflecting upon these mysterious factors, and bringing them within reach of human comprehension.

arxiv-2003-05398.title: Stratification of polymer-colloid mixtures via fast nonequilibrium evaporation
arxiv-2003-05398.creator: Kyoungmun Lee, Siyoung Q. Choi
arxiv-2003-05398.description: Abstract In drying liquid films of polymer-colloid mixtures, the stratification in which polymers are placed on top of larger colloids is studied. It is often presumed that the formation of segregated polymer-colloid layers is solely due to the proportion in size at fast evaporation as in binary colloid mixtures.

arxiv-2101-11756.title: A note on tight projective 2 2 -designs
arxiv-2101-11756.creator: Joseph W. Iverson, Emily J. King, Dustin G. Mixon
arxiv-2101-11756.description: Abstract We study tight projective 2 2 -designs in three different settings. In the complex setting, Zauner’s conjecture predicts the existence of a tight projective 2 2 -design in every dimension. Pandey, Paulsen, Prakash, and Rahaman recently proposed an approach to make quantitative progress on this conjecture in terms of the entanglement breaking rank of a certain quantum channel.

arxiv-2104-06205.title: Explicit breather solution of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation
arxiv-2104-06205.creator: Robert Conte
arxiv-2104-06205.description: Abstract We present a one-line closed form expression for the three-parameter breather of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation. This provides an analytic proof of the time period doubling observed in experiments. The experimental check that some pulses generated in optical fibers are indeed such generalized breathers will be drastically simplified.

arxiv-2108-04067.title: Machine learning for predicting the B z {}_{\textrm{z}} magnetic field component from upstream in situ observations of solar coronal mass ejections
arxiv-2108-04067.description: Abstract Predicting the B z {}_{\textrm{z}} magnetic field embedded within ICMEs, also known as the B z {}_{\textrm{z}} problem, is a key challenge in space weather forecasting. We study the hypothesis that upstream in situ measurements of the sheath region and the first few hours of the magnetic obstacle provide sufficient information for predicting the downstream B z {}_{\textrm{z}} component.

arxiv-2108-13030.title: Lithium Evolution of Giant Stars Observed by LAMOST and Kepler
arxiv-2108-13030.creator: Jinghua Zhang, Jian-Rong Shi, Hong-Liang Yan, Yaguang Li, Qi Gao, Chun-Qian Li, Xianfei Zhang, Shuai Liu, Shaolan Bi, Gang Zhao, Yan Li
arxiv-2108-13030.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jinghua Zhang, Jian-Rong Shi, Hong-Liang Yan, Yaguang Li, Qi Gao, Chun-Qian Li, Xianfei Zhang, Shuai Liu, Shaolan Bi, Gang Zhao, Yan Li. Mapping lithium evolution for evolved stars will provide restrictions and constraints on the fundamental stellar interior physical processes, which further shed light on our understanding of the theory of stellar structure and evolution.

arxiv-2206-00097.title: Real-time motion planning and decision-making for a group of differential drive robots under connectivity constraints using robust MPC and mixed-integer programming
arxiv-2206-00097.creator: Angelo Caregnato-Neto a , Marcos O. A. Maximo b and Rubens J. M. Afonso a
arxiv-2206-00097.description: Abstract This work is concerned with the problem of planning trajectories and assigning tasks for a Multi-Agent System (MAS) comprised of differential drive robots. We propose a multirate hierarchical control structure that employs a planner based on robust Model Predictive Control (MPC) with mixed-integer programming (MIP) encoding.

arxiv-2302-02177.title: Towards a modeling, optimization and predictive control framework for fed-batch metabolic cybergenetics
arxiv-2302-02177.creator: Sebastián Espinel-Ríos, Bruno Morabito, Johannes Pohlodek, Katja Bettenbrock, Steffen Klamt, Rolf Findeisen
arxiv-2302-02177.description: Abstract Biotechnology offers many opportunities for the sustainable manufacturing of valuable products. The toolbox to optimize bioprocesses includes extracellular process elements such as the bioreactor design and mode of operation, medium formulation, culture conditions, feeding rates, etc. However, these elements are frequently insufficient for achieving optimal process performance or precise product composition.

arxiv-2311-03646.title: Secondary Lepton Production, Propagation, and Interactions with NuLeptonSim
arxiv-2311-03646.creator: Austin Cummings, Ryan Krebs, Stephanie Wissel, Jaime Alvarez-Muñiz, Washington R. Carvalho Jr, Andrés Romero-Wolf, Harm Schoorlemmer, Enrique Zas
arxiv-2311-03646.description: Abstract Charged current interactions of neutrinos inside the Earth can result in secondary muons and τ \tau -leptons which are detectable by several existing and planned neutrino experiments through a wide variety of event topologies. Consideration of such events can improve detector performance and provide unique signatures which help with event reconstruction.

arxiv-2403-13010.title: A Dual-Tier Adaptive One-Class Classification IDS for Emerging Cyberthreats Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
arxiv-2403-13010.creator: Md. Ashraf Uddin, Sunil Aryal, Mohamed Reda Bouadjenek, Muna Al-Hawawreh, Md. Alamin Talukder
arxiv-2403-13010.description: Abstract In today’s digital age, our dependence on IoT (Internet of Things) and IIoT (Industrial IoT) systems has grown immensely, which facilitates sensitive activities such as banking transactions and personal, enterprise data, and legal document exchanges. Cyberattackers consistently exploit weak security measures and tools. The Network Intrusion Detection System (IDS) acts as a primary tool against such cyber threats.

arxiv-2410-04173.title: Fast Object Detection with a Machine Learning Edge Device
arxiv-2410-04173.creator: Richard C. Rodriguez, MSDA, Jonah Elijah P. Bardos, MS
arxiv-2410-04173.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Richard C. Rodriguez, MSDA, Jonah Elijah P. Bardos, MS. This machine learning study investigates a low-cost edge device integrated with an embedded system having computer vision and resulting in an improved performance in inferencing time and precision of object detection and classification.

arxiv-2411-02127.title: Supervised Transfer Learning Framework for Fault Diagnosis in Wind Turbines
arxiv-2411-02127.creator: Kenan Weber, Christine Preisach
arxiv-2411-02127.description: Abstract Common challenges in fault diagnosis include the lack of labeled data and the need to build models for each domain, resulting in many models that require supervision. Transfer learning can help tackle these challenges by learning cross-domain knowledge. Many approaches still require at least some labeled data in the target domain, and often provide unexplainable results.

arxiv-2501-05696.title: Combinatorial identities related to degenerate Stirling numbers of the second kind
arxiv-2501-05696.creator: Dae San Kim, Taekyun Kim
arxiv-2501-05696.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Dae San Kim, Taekyun Kim. The study of degenerate versions of certain special polynomials and numbers, which was initiated by Carlitz’s work on degenerate Euler and degenerate Bernoulli polynomials, has recently seen renewed interest among mathematicians. The aim of this paper is to study some properties, certain identities, recurrence relations and explicit expressions for degenerate Stirling numbers of the second kind, which are a degenerate version of the Stirling numbers of the second kind.

arxiv-2507-21520.title: Solution for Meta KDD Cup’ 25: A Comprehensive Three-Step Framework for Vision Question Answering Conference: 2025 KDD Cup Workshop for Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation; ; ISBN: CCS: Computing methodologies Natural language generation
arxiv-2507-21520.creator: Zijian Zhang, Xiaocheng Zhang, Yang Zhou, Zhimin Lin, Peng Yan
arxiv-2507-21520.description: Abstract . Vision Large Language Models (VLLMs) have improved multi-modal understanding and visual question answering (VQA), but still suffer from hallucinated answers. Multi-modal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) helps address these issues by incorporating external information, yet challenges remain in visual context comprehension, multi-source retrieval, and multi-turn interactions.

arxiv-2507-22028.title: From Seeing to Experiencing: Scaling Navigation Foundation Models with Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2507-22028.creator: Honglin He, Yukai Ma, Wayne Wu, Bolei ZhouUniversity of California, Los Angeles https://metadriverse.github.io/s2e
arxiv-2507-22028.description: Abstract Navigation foundation models trained on massive web-scale data enable agents to generalize across diverse environments and embodiments. However, these models, which are trained solely on offline data, often lack the capacity to reason about the consequences of their actions or adapt through counterfactual understanding.

arxiv-2511-23237.title: Systems that saturate the Margolus–Levitin quantum speed limit
arxiv-2511-23237.creator: Ole Sönnerborn
arxiv-2511-23237.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ole Sönnerborn. We provide a complete characterization of all finite-dimensional quantum states that saturate the Margolus–Levitin quantum speed limit at arbitrary Uhlmann–Jozsa fidelity. Employing a purification-based approach, we prove that mixed-state saturation occurs precisely when three structural criteria are fulfilled: the state’s support is confined to the sum of two energy eigenspaces (the ground level and a single excited level); each eigenvector of the state with nonzero weight is a fixed superposition of one ground- and one excited-state energy eigenvector (determined by the minimizer

europmc-pmc6451800.creator: Aimar A, Palermo A, Innocenti B.
europmc-pmc6451800.description: Three-dimensional (3D) printing refers to a number of manufacturing technologies that generate a physical model from digital information. plos-pone-0012678.creator: Qin Li, Feng Zhang, Xin Li et al.
plos-pone-0012678.description: PLOS ONE research article. It is well known that genetic components play an important role in the etiology of mandibular prognathism, but few susceptibility loci have been mapped. In order to identify linkage regions for mandibular prognathism, we analyzed two Chinese pedigrees with 6,090 genome-wide singl

pmc-10646620.title: Relative fat fraction of malignant bone lesions from breast cancer, prostate cancer and myeloma are significantly lower than normal bone marrow and shows excellent interobserver agreement
pmc-10646620.creator: Francesca Castagnoli, Ricardo Donners, Nina Tunariu, Christina Messiou, Dow-Mu Koh
pmc-10646620.description: ObjectivesTo compare relative fat fraction (rFF) of active bone lesions from breast, prostate and myeloma malignancies and normal bone marrow; to assess its inter-reader agreement.MethodsPatients with breast (n = 26), myeloma (n = 32) and prostate cancer (n = 52) were retrospectively evaluated. 110 baseline rFF maps from whole-body MRI were reviewed by two radiologists.

pmc-10736484.title: WHAT DOES IT MEAN TO REST? A STUDY OF CAREGIVERS CARING FOR A PERSON WITH DEMENTIA
pmc-10736484.creator: Sarah Hahn
pmc-10736484.description: The number of informal caregivers caring for a person with dementia (PWD) has been increasing steadily over the past decade; more than 11 million Americans provide unpaid care as of 2022 (Alzheimer’s Association, 2022). The impact of caregiving is immense; caregivers risk having chronic health issues, poor emotional well-being, and physiological changes (Alzheimer’s Association, 2022).

pmc-11352454.title: Engineered species-selective ion-exchange in tuneable dual-phase zeolite composites†
pmc-11352454.creator: James L. A. Reed, Andrew James, Thomas Carey, Neelam Fitzgerald, Simon Kellet, Antony Nearchou, Adele L. Farrelly, Harrison A. H. Fell, Phoebe K. Allan, Joseph A. Hriljac
pmc-11352454.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Controllable sorption selectivity in zeolites is crucial for their application in catalysis, gas separation and ion-exchange. Whilst existing approaches to achieving sorption selectivity with natural zeolites typically rely on screening for specific geological deposits, here we develop partial interzeolite transformation as a straightforward and highly tuneable method to achieve sorption selectivity via forming dual-phase composites with simultaneous control of both phase-ratio and morphology.

pmc-11644894.title: Benefits of Using Design Patterns on Microcontrollers in Implemented IoT Applications
pmc-11644894.creator: Marek Babiuch, Petr Foltynek
pmc-11644894.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). As part of our research for microcontroller software support, we have developed a modular framework that utilizes previously unimplemented architectural principles for developing applications on microcontrollers. These principles are still a privilege of enterprise and server applications. The paper describes the benefits of a new architectural approach to developing applications on microcontrollers and describes the most common application scenarios along with examples of IoT application development using a framework with design pattern architecture and SOLID principles.

pmc-13181902.title: Curcumin inhibits chondrocyte apoptosis and inflammation in osteoarthritis via the miR-338-3p/EIF4A1 signaling axis
pmc-13181902.creator: Na Dai, Bin Shi
pmc-13181902.description: ObjectiveOsteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disorder mainly characterized by articular cartilage degradation. Curcumin, the primary bioactive compound derived from turmeric, exhibits anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and anti-catabolic activities. This study aimed to explore the therapeutic potential of curcumin in OA and its underlying mechanism involving the microRNA-338-3p (miR-338-3p)/Eukaryotic Translation Initiation Factor 4A1 (EIF4A1) signaling pathway.

pmc-13354731.title: Psychedelics and neurostimulation for treatment resistant psychiatric disorders
pmc-13354731.creator: Filip Blazek, Klara Latalova, David Krahulik, Lumir Hrabalek
pmc-13354731.description: Psychedelic-assisted therapy and neurostimulation represent converging approaches to modulating dysfunctional brain circuits in treatment-resistant psychiatric disorders. This Perspective outlines shared mechanisms involving neuroplasticity and network reconfiguration, and examines ethical, regulatory, and infrastructural barriers to their translation. Bridging neuroscience, psychiatry, and policy, it proposes strategies for integrating these innovative interventions into evidence-based, circuit-focused models of mental health care.

pmc-13361986.title: Effects of dexmedetomidine vs. magnesium sulfate on hemodynamics in spine surgeries: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13361986.creator: Eman Mohamed Teema, Ahmed Oun, Bassma Raslan, Sara Helmy, Mohamed K. Elghobashy, Omima Samaha, Aiman Al-Touny
pmc-13361986.description: BackgroundBlood loss and hemodynamic instability are common challenges in spine surgery, often managed with controlled hypotension. Dexmedetomidine (DEX), a selective α2-adrenoceptor agonist, and magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄), an NMDA receptor antagonist and calcium channel blocker, are commonly used for this purpose, but their comparative efficacy and safety remain unclear.

pmc-13503939.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of hemorrhoid patients regarding surgical treatment
pmc-13503939.creator: Yan Hu, Xihong Wang, Lihong Chen
pmc-13503939.description: This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of patients with hemorrhoids concerning surgical treatment. This cross-sectional study was conducted between October 2023 and February 2025 in Chengdu, Sichuan Province, China and included patients diagnosed with hemorrhoids.

pmc-13621703.title: Biochar and ZnO-Se nanocomposites enhanced biochemical and antioxidant profiling of soybean: insight into GC-MS metabolomics, and KEGG pathway analysis
pmc-13621703.creator: Ubaidur Rahman, Maaz Ahmad, Zohaib Younas, Ilyas Ahmad, Mohammad Hamid Hamdard, Zia-ur-Rehman Mashwani
pmc-13621703.description: Soybean (Glycine max L.) is a significant oilseed crop that is frequently limited by soil fertility, micronutrient deficiencies and oxidative stress. Although biochar and nano enable micronutrients have individually been reported to improve crop performance. There synergistic effect on the biochemical traits, antioxidants defense, and metabolic reactions of soybean have not yet been explored.
